m: नम् cl. 1. P. नमति (Dhātup. xxiii, 12), ˚ते (mostly intrans.; cf. Pāṇ. iii, 1, 89; pr. p. Ā. नमान, R.; pf. P. नानाम or ननाम, RV. &c.; 2. sg. नेमिथ, or ननन्थ, Vop.; Subj. ननमस्, RV.; 3. pl. नेमुर्, Kāv.; Ā. नेमे, RV.; 3. pl. -ननामिरे, MBh.; aor. P. अनान्, Kāṭh.; अनंसीत्, Daś.; Ā. अनंस्त Gr.; 3. pl. अनंसत, Br.; Subj. नंसै, नंसन्ते, RV.; fut. नंस्यति, Br.; नमिष्यति, Hariv.; नन्ता, Siddh.; inf. -नमम्, -नमे, RV.; नन्तुम्, नमितुम्, Kāv.; ind.p. नत्वा, BhP.; Kathās.; -नत्य, Br.; -नम्य, MBh.) to bend or bow (either trans. or oftener intr.), to bow to, subject or submit one's self (with gen. dat. or acc.), RV. &c. &c.; (with हिरुक्) to turn away, keep aside, AV. iv, 1, 3; to turn towards i.e. to aim at (gen.) with (instr.), RV. i, 165, 6; to yield or give way, keep quiet or be silent, Bālar. vi, 12; (in gram.) to change a dental letter into a cerebral, RPrāt. : Pass. नम्यते, to be bent or bowed; yield or submit to, TUp. iii, 10, 4 : Caus. नमयति, RV. &c. &c. (नामयति, Up. &c.; नाम्यति [!] Mṛcch. i, 30; aor. अनीनमत्, RV.; Pass. नाम्यते, ˚ति, MBh. &c.) to cause to bow or sink, incline, RV. &c. &c.; (with चापम्) to bend a bow, MBh.; Hariv. &c.; to turn away or ward off, RV.; to aim at (gen.), ix, 97, 15; (in gram.) to change a dental letter into a cerebral, RPrāt. : Desid. निनंसति, Gr. : Intens. नन्नमीति, RV.; नन्नम्यते, KātyŚr. (3. sg. नम्नते impf. अनम्नत, p. नममान, RV.) to bow or submit one's self to (dat.), RV.; Br.
नम् [cf. Zd. nam, nemaiti; Gk. νέμω, νέμος, νόμος; Lat. nemus; Goth., Old Sax., Angl.Sax. niman; HGerm. nëman, nëmen, nehmen.]
a: नम् — {c1c} P., sometimes A. (नमति-ते, ननाम, अनंसीत्, नंस्यति, नत; caus. नमयति-ते or नामयति-ते, but with a preposition नमयति only; desid. निनंसति) 1 To bow to, make obeisance to, salute (as a mark of respect) (with acc. or dat.); इयं नमति वः सर्वान् त्रिलोचनवधूरिति Ku. 6. 89; Bg. 11. 37; Bk. 9. 51, 10. 31; 12. 39; Śi. 4. 57. --2 To submit or subject oneself, bow down; अशक्तः संधिमान् नमेत् Kām. 8. 55. --3 To bend, sink; go down; अनंसीद्भूर्भरेणास्य Bk. 15. 25. नेमुः सर्वदिशः K. 55; उन्नमति नमति वर्षति…मेघः Mk. 5. 26. --4 To stoop, be inclined. --5 To be bent or curved. --6 To sound. --7 To change a dental to a lingual letter. --Caus. 1 To bend, make curved. --2 To bend (as a bow); Ś. 2. 3. --3 To cause to sink. --4 To prevent, ward off.

a: नमस् — ind. 1 A bow, salutation, obeisance, adoration; (this word is, by itself, invariably used with dat.; तस्मै वदान्यगुरवे तरवे नमोऽस्तु Bv. 1. 94; नमस्त्रिमूर्तये तुभ्यं Ku. 2. 4; but with कृ, generally with acc.; मुनित्रयं नमस्कृत्य Sk.; but sometimes with dat. also; नमस्कुर्मो नृसिंहाय ibid. The word has the sense of a noun, but is treated as an indeclinable.) --2 Ved. Food. --3 A thunderbolt. --4 A gift, present. --5 A sacrifice. --Comp. --कारः, --कृतिः f. --करणं bowing, respectful or reverential salutation, respectful obeisance (made by uttering the word नमस्). --कृत a. {1} bowed down to, saluted. {2} revered, adored, worshipped. --गुरुः {1} a spiritual teacher. {2} a Brāhmaṇa. --वाकं ind. uttering the word नमस्, i. e. making a low obeisance; इदं कविभ्यः पूर्वेभ्यो नमोवाकं प्रशास्महे U. 1. 1. --वृध् m. a sacrifice.

a: नमुचिः — [न मुंचति] 1 N. of a demon slain by Indra; वनमुचे नमुचेररये शिरः R. 9. 22. [When Indra conquered the Asuras, there was only one called Namuci who strongly resisted and at last captured him. He offered to let Indra go provided he promised ‘not to kill by day or by night, with wet or dry’. Indra promised to do so and was released, but he cut off Namuci's head at twilight and with foam of water (which is neither wet nor dry). According to another version Namuci was a friend of Indra, and once drank up his strength and made him quite imbecile. The Aśvins (and Sarasvatī also, as the story goes) then supplied Indra with a Vajra with which he cut off the demon's head]. --2 N. of the god of love. --Comp. --सूदनः, --द्विष् --हन् m. epithets of Indra.
